title: Product KPI catalog dispatch backlog — G0-003
required_human_authorities: Product Owner review for G0-003 metric formula, source, owner and any target
Accountant and Privacy/Legal review before any applicable later A6 commercial or retention conclusion
purpose: Record the source-defined G0-003 dispatch backlog within the A6 production-readiness lane. The first safe slice is a synthetic metric dictionary that keeps every KPI target pending Product Owner approval; later A6 deliverables require separately recorded expert decisions and routing.

include: G0-003 metric name, business purpose, formula, unit, denominator, owner, future source and synthetic edge cases
The source-defined A0+A6 ownership and Product review route for G0-003
Explicit routing of later A6 risk, retention, secret, billing, incident, restore and release work without accepting that later scope
exclude: KPI target approval, vanity targets, customer data, event instrumentation, database schema, migrations, provider calls, Stripe or Meta credentials, production configuration, legal/tax/accounting conclusions and Gate G0 approval

ownership.forbidden_paths_note: The globs **/*secret* and **/*credential* were removed: they forbade this package's own declared outputs (the secret scanner and its test), a contradiction the ownership validator could not see until it began comparing outputs against forbidden_paths. Replaced with the extensions that carry actual key material. A filename mentioning "secret" is not a secret; a private key file is.

acceptance_criteria: The backlog packet preserves the source-defined WP-0A-A6-001 scope and maps G0-003 to a synthetic-only first slice.
No role is assigned or package status advanced until a real capability declaration and distinct author, reviewer, tester and integration IDs are independently verified.
Every KPI target remains pending Product Owner approval; no instrumentation, schema, provider or customer-data change is authorized.
required_tests: Work-package JSON, role-separation and ownership validators
Repository canonical check before any dispatch commit
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. This package range covers work-packages/WP-0A-A6-001.json, five files under evidence/WP-0A-A6-001/ and one handoff: a specification document, its reading view and two read-only checkers. Reverting removes the G0-003 metric dictionary and returns the CTR-OBS-001 per-label cardinality budget to having no home, and removes nothing else -- no target was set to un-set, no contract artifact was changed to restore, and no event, schema, migration, provider call or customer record exists to roll back. A forward fix is preferable for any single wrong metric entry, because the entries are independent of one another. The withdrawn increment on agent/claude/WP-0A-A6-001-product-kpi-catalog is unaffected by either: it is read-only input and is not on this branch.
open_blockers: A6 has not yet supplied an independently reviewed capability benchmark for billing-cost-ops; it must not be assigned as Author from its current declaration.
OPEN-016 requires Product Owner review for every metric formula, source, owner and any target before G0-003 can close; targets remain pending.

Product Owner is the G0-003 reviewer. Accountant, Privacy/Legal and Security authorities are mandatory for applicable later A6 subscopes and cannot be represented by an agent skill-profile placeholder.

DISPOSITION 2026-09-03, by the Product Owner, of the staffing defect this package recorded. The defect is A0's, not the Author's: A0 assigned against blockers[0] in this very manifest, and the Author noticed, refused to paper over it, recorded it, and did the work under protest. RFC-2026-013 settles the principle -- role legitimacy is keyed to what a capability profile declares an agent may hold, and cc-a6-relay.json declares review only. The artifact on branch agent/claude/WP-0A-A6-001-product-kpi-catalog is REVIEWED INPUT, not an author-attested deliverable, and /claude/a6_relay is credited as its source. Re-staffing requires: a forward-scoped billing-cost-ops capability benchmark for that run, produced by a run distinct from it and from its reviewer; the six changes the independent review required; and a fresh authorship act that addresses them. Evidence: evidence/WP-0A-A6-001/independent-review-and-staffing-defect.md. The branch declaration is withdrawn with the assignment: a package declares a branch to own the work on it as its own attested output, and this package does not. The commits are not deleted -- they are the input the next authorship act starts from. There is no protocol state for 'work exists, authorship withdrawn', and backlog with no branch is the closest honest one. This entry disposes of blockers[0] and [4] for the FUTURE only -- neither is deleted, because a benchmark written after an assignment cannot un-perform it.

INTEGRATION-RECORDED 2026-09-03 by /claude/r0_steward, Integration Owner. C-01 STATES TWO DIFFERENT FORMULAS AND THE PACKAGE CANNOT GO TO done UNTIL IT STATES ONE. Its formula is decimal_sum(cost.amount) over the population grouped by cost.currency, divided by count(distinct attribution.workspace_id), with NO `grouping` -- which yields one FLEET number per currency per month: total cost over how many workspaces there were. Its definition, "Provider cost attributed to a workspace over a month", reads as a figure belonging to ONE workspace. A-01 shows the shape that disambiguates: it declares `grouping: tenant_context.workspace_id` and is therefore evaluated once per workspace. The Reviewer found this and approved with it open; the Integration Owner reproduced it independently and records it here rather than passing it on in prose. Three things make it more than a wording slip. The unit, "decimal money string, per currency", sheds the workspace dimension the denominator introduces -- contrast A-04, which has the same fleet-mean shape and whose unit and definition BOTH read as a mean, so A-04 is internally consistent and C-01 is not. The caveat, "THERE IS NO SINGLE-NUMBER COST PER WORKSPACE", is about currency and reads as though there would otherwise BE a per-workspace number, leaning against its own formula. And it is the money metric, whose owner line already requires Accountant review under OPEN-001: a fleet mean is exactly the figure a reader mistakes for what a workspace costs. IT DOES NOT BLOCK INTEGRATION -- nothing is instrumented, the target is null, and OPEN-016 already routes every formula through Product Owner review before G0-003 closes. IT BLOCKS done, because a metric dictionary that states a formula ambiguously has failed at the one thing it is for, and this must not reach the Product Owner as one formula to approve while it is two. CLOSING IT IS A CORRECTIVE AUTHORSHIP ACT, not an integration act: the Author decides whether the intent is a fleet mean (then fix the definition, the key and the unit) or a per-workspace figure (then add `grouping: attribution.workspace_id` and drop the denominator). The Integration Owner holds no Author authority and did not edit the entry. Evidence: evidence/WP-0A-A6-001/integration-verdict.md, residual 1.

INTEGRATION-RECORDED 2026-09-03 by /claude/r0_steward. Two limitations found at integration, NEITHER blocking integration, both to be carried into the next authorship act rather than rediscovered. (1) M-10 DECLINES TO CHOOSE AND TWO ENTRIES QUIETLY CHOOSE, DIFFERENTLY. M-10 correctly leaves open whether a superseding CTR-USG-001 record reuses the superseded record’s `occurred_at` or carries its own, and routes the question to that contract’s owner. But it claims the populations are "stated in a form that is correct under both readings", and the restatement PROSE is not neutral: C-01 says a closed period restates "upward when it is replaced by a larger one", which happens only if the replacement lands in the SAME month; A-04 says a correction "removes the record it supersedes from that month’s population, so the month’s figure changes", which changes a COUNT only if the replacement is NOT added back to that month. The population BLOCKS are correct under both readings; these two sentences are not, and M-10’s "correct under both" is broader than what holds. Whoever answers M-10 must fix both sentences; whoever touches them first must make them neutral rather than pick a reading. (2) A COST AGGREGATE THAT OMITS ITS `population` BLOCK ENTIRELY PASSES BOTH CHECKERS GREEN. Reproduced: deleting C-03’s whole `population` block -- C-03 being a decimal_sum(cost.amount) aggregate over CTR-USG-001, exactly the class condition C2 governs -- leaves verify-source-fields.mjs AND population-and-carrier-probes.mjs both at exit 0 reporting "no problems". The checker validates that a STATED population covers all three axes and has no rule that one must EXIST. The only trace is the summary count sliding from "6 carrying a stated population" to 5, and unlike "63 field path(s) (pinned at 63)" that count is not pinned. So the defect C2 exists to prevent is the one shape the guard cannot see. This is a FOURTH entry on the Tester’s list of checker limitations, not a fifth defect in the dictionary: every entry in the tree does carry its population, and the guard would not have caught it if one did not. The fix is to pin the population count the way the field count is pinned, or to require a population on every CTR-USG-001 aggregate. Recorded here because the Integration Owner cannot add it to the checker’s own limitation list without authoring. Evidence: evidence/WP-0A-A6-001/integration-verdict.md, residuals 2 and 3.
